issue_context.title: Flag to ban old control flow directive (ngFor, ngIf etc)
issue_context.body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

_No response_

### Description

After migrating to new control flow logic, any developer can just accidentally start using the old syntax again. 

### Proposed solution

Have a flag that allows instances of `*ngFor`, `*ngIf` to be banned from use and have this flagged in the compiler and vscode extension.

### Alternatives considered

n/a
comments: This sounds like a job for [Angular ESLint](https://github.com/angular-eslint/angular-eslint).

It sounds like a deprecation warning for angular... why would a linter enforce a framework specific change?

Side note: I avoid eslint like the plague due to its terrible performance profile and use biomejs instead

> It sounds like a deprecation warning for angular... why would a linter enforce a framework specific change?
> 
> Side note: I avoid eslint like the plague due to its terrible performance profile and use biomejs instead

Omg that project looks awesome, why didn't I know about this? Sorry for the spam guys

If you want to ban control flow today, and are willing to use ESLint, you can use the [`@angular-eslint/template/prefer-control-flow` rule from Angular ESLint](https://github.com/angular-eslint/angular-eslint/blob/main/packages/eslint-plugin-template/docs/rules/prefer-control-flow.md).
A ESLint rule, as suggested by @json-derulo is what we would recommend if you want prevent a project from using directive-based control flow after migration.
